newsitem.title: UK: NWE fuel oil - tenders support tight market.
newsitem.headline: NWE fuel oil - tenders support tight market.

text.p: High and low sulphur cracked fuel prices edged up $1-2 on Friday as support from the latest Portuguese and Tunisian buy tenders began to bite.
"Swaps are not moving much, but prompt wet barrels are not easy to find," said one trader who saw further gains next week.
"If I had a cargo, I won't be selling for less than $110 fob NWE," said a trader at a major.
Activity in the cargo market was flat since potential sellers with product were looking to sell any material to the winners of the 150,000-tonne Portuguese tender.
A Tunisian requirement for two extra cargoes into Bizerte in
October in addition to the 200,000 tender that runs from October to January was also bullish.
The low sulphur cracked sector was also looking stronger amidst renewed industry talk that the main Med buyer, which picked up a cargo at $124.75 cif Milazzo yesterday, was in the market today.

"With supplies tight and the buyer more active prices should hold next week," a trader said. The threat of Caribbean material heading into the Med was a bullish factor, but nothing definite has been done. Prices in NWE were assessed around $120 fob NWE.
